text:
Clear skies and a light breeze have us in the low 50s already, and we're on track for a really nice afternoon. Expect the high to land around 61, maybe a few degrees warmer if the sun holds. Some high clouds will drift in later as a cold front approaches, but they won't spoil anything. If you want to see the last of the fall color, this is the day. A light jacket will do until the sun gets going, and the sun sets just before 6.

Tonight turns partly cloudy and not as cold as recent nights, with a low around 40. Monday stays mild with a high near 60 and a mix of sun and clouds. There's a slight chance of a shower around 3 or 4 in the afternoon, but the air is so dry that most of us will stay dry, and I wouldn't change plans.

The real change comes Tuesday, when highs only reach the 40s, and Wednesday morning could bring the coldest air of the season. Bring in anything tender before then.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-25T10:36:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Mild temperatures expected today and Monday ahead of an approaching cold front.
  2. Cooler temperatures expected Sunday with warming temperatures through the remainder of the week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 212 AM EDT Sunday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Today will be a chamber of commerce type of day with high temperatures warming into the lower to mid 60s after a cool start to the morning. Light winds will switch to the south at 5-12 mph this afternoon. Plentiful sunshine will be seen through much of the day with high clouds filtering in ahead of the approaching cold front this afternoon. A cold front will move across the region Monday afternoon with the potential for isolated to scattered rain showers ahead of the boundary. Models continue to show a plethora of dry air in the low levels and the general idea is that the best chances for rain will be across the high terrain as it's unlikely we see the deeper valleys have time to saturate before dry air advects into the region in the wake of the cold front. Some of the high-res guidance is showing up to 0.05" of rain across the summits but even that seems a bit generous given the antecedent dry air mass. KEY MESSAGE 2: Noticeably colder temperatures will be observed on Tuesday and Wednesday as high pressure and clear skies will coincide with decent low level cold advection. Tuesday morning will see lows in the 20s while Wednesday morning will see lows in the lower teens to lower 20s. Highs on Tuesday will only climb into the 40s. It'll be our first real taste of arctic air this fall as the transition to winter isn't too far away. As a matter of fact, we may be looking at some record low temperatures Wednesday morning. The good news is that high pressure overhead will allow the air mass to slowly moderate Wednesday into next weekend with highs climbing back into the 60s for Thursday and Friday. There is a slight chance for a few showers on Friday with another weak cold front but again it looks like dry conditions will likely persist. For those with little ones who plan to go trick-or-treating, the forecast for Halloween looks dry and seasonably mild.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Today will continue the dry and sunny weather, except it will be pleasantly warmer with highs in the upper 50s to mid-60s. It will be excellent for checking out the remaining fall foliage. Though we’re past peak at this point, there are still some trees that have nice color. Tonight won’t be as cold due to a gentle southwest breeze ahead of a cold front. That front will pass through mainly dry on Monday, but a few sprinkles are possible in northern parts of the region. Highs will be in the 50s. Much cooler air will move in behind this front. Tuesday will be a nice-looking day, but it will be quite chilly with highs only in the 40s. You’ll certainly want a jacket. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are likely. Wednesday will be a bit warmer with sunny skies and highs in the upper 40s to low 50s. Thursday will be pleasant with some low 60s expected. Another front will move through Thursday night. Some showers are possible along that, but no significant rain is expected. Any showers will end Friday morning, with the rest of the day being partly sunny and fair. Halloween looks good for trick-or-treaters with mostly sunny skies and highs mainly in the mid-50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-25T13:26:00Z — same caveat): Sunny and warmer Sunday, after another frosty start — High pressure stays nearby Sunday, bringing full sunshine! It turns warmer, thanks to a light south breeze that develops. Highs reach the mid-60s. Clouds increase tonight, and it will be seasonably cold with patchy frost. Lows will be near 40 in the Champlain Valley, but most towns fall to the upper 20s and 30s. After some early rays of sun, Monday turns mostly cloudy with a few spot showers in northern areas, due to a cold front on approach. Highs reach the upper 50s there. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall, where highs again push well into the 60s. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable north breeze. Wednesday starts with another widespread freeze, but it turns seasonable by afternoon, with highs in the low 50s and a mostly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs near 60, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely Thursday night into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs reach the low 60s.
